title: Per-conversation microeconomics and SME pricing doodles
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad to explore per-conversation (per-convo) economics for small / SMB style customers and a few ‘SME’ packaging ideas. Informal, lots of approximations — meant to feed a short sync with product/growth.

Context / assumptions (baseline):
- Reference model: 7B-ish open-ish model (quantized runtime) used as the low-latency default.
- GPU cost (fully loaded): $3.50 / GPU-hour for a shared cluster amortized (post-discounts).
- Serving throughput (realistic): ~150 tokens/s per GPU for steady generation (varies a lot by opt).
- Avg request pattern (target product): short interactive convos, 6 user messages, 6 model turns, 1.2k tokens generated total per session on avg.
- KV / prefix cache hit assumed: 35% for repeat-ish flows (chat resumes); higher for chatbots with memory.
- Extra infra overhead (routing, logging, permissive retries): add ~12% to token compute cost.

Back-of-napkin token cost per convo:
- Tokens generated: 1,200 tokens (avg). + user tokens (prompt) say 350 tokens total input = 1,550 tokens per convo.
- Effective tokens after caching/batching savings: assume 20% reduction overall => 1,240 billed-equivalent tokens.
- Tokens per GPU-hour: 150 tokens/s * 3600s = 540k tokens/hr.
- GPU cost per token: $3.50 / 540k = $0.00000648 per token (~0.0000065).
- Token compute cost per convo: 1,240 * 0.0000065 ≈ $0.0081.
- Add infra overhead (12%): $0.00097 => subtotal $0.0091.
- Margin and packaging buffer: want gross margin >= 70% on hosted PAYG => retail per-convo price >= $0.0091 / 0.30 ≈ $0.030.
- Rounded target: $0.03 per convo as pure PAYG floor for 7B baseline.

Sensitivity checks (quick):
- If avg generation is 600 tokens instead of 1200 => per-convo price halves (~$0.015).
- If GPU cost is $6/hr (dedicated/reserved worse case) => compute cost doubles => retail ~ $0.06.
- Cache hit improves from 20% reduction to 40% => token usage 930 => retail ~ $0.022.

Other per-convo overheads to consider (not included above):
- Network egress/ingress (tiny for text unless multimodal).
- Customer-specific encryption/KMS extra charges for Private deploys.
- Support & onboarding amortization (for small customers maybe $X/mo).
- SLA / standby capacity for low-latency (cost uplift for reserved concurrency slots).

Packaging ideas derived from the math:
1) Micro-payg (per-convo credit):
   - Sell conversation credits (packs of 1k/5k/20k convos).
   - Unit price anchored at $0.025–$0.04 per convo depending on pack.
   - Pack discount logic: 1k @ 3.5c, 5k @ 3c, 20k @ 2.5c (encourages commitment).
   - Pros: simple mental model for product teams with low-interaction volumes.
   - Cons: conversations vary a lot in token size — need cap or conversion table (tokens => convos).

2) Session-bundles (timeboxed sessions):
   - Sell bundles in 'active minutes' (e.g., 100 active minutes = N convos typical).
   - Useful for interactive demos / sales enablement and instructor-type workflows.

3) Micro-subscription + top-ups (hybrid):
   - $29/mo includes 1k convos + PAYG at 2.5c above that.
   - Higher tiers give lower per-convo PAYG and concurrency boosts.
   - This smooths revenue and reduces churn risk vs pure PAYG.

4) SLA-backed low-latency premium:
   - Base customers get best-effort. Low-latency SLO (<200ms p95) add-on +20–40% price.
   - Map to reserved compute + dedicated buckets.

5) Pack by intent (intent-weighted pricing):
   - Conversational types classified by token-intensity: micro (avg <300 tokens), standard (300–1200), longform (>1200).
   - Sell micro-bundles cheaper per convo; longer conversation classes priced higher or priced by token.

Operational considerations / gates:
- Need an accurate token-to-convo mapping in billing (either compute tokens directly or set conservative average tokens per convo per customer).
- Fraud / abuse controls if small packs are cheap — rate limits and anomaly detection.
- UI UX: show predicted tokens per convo to customer during onboarding or in billing page.
- Credits expiration policy — short expiration increases revenue capture but annoys users.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to account for multi-model routing? If we route low-cost traffic to 7B and heavy-lift to 13B/70B fallbacks, how to represent pack consumption? Idea: tiered consumption where 7B convos consume 1 credit, 13B convos 1.8 credits, etc. Need conversion table.
- Can we bake a small per-convo minimum (e.g., 0.5c) to prevent extremely short spammy calls affecting economics?
- How to expose cache savings to customers? Option: sell "sticky-session" add-on that guarantees prefix cache warmness for returning sessions (good for assistants).
- Measure real distribution: P95 token per convo, median, 90th — need telemetry to set pack sizes and protect margins.

Notes for next steps before sharing with PMs:
- Pull real telemetry: avg tokens / convo, sessions/day, KV hit distribution for top 20 beta users.
- Run sensitivity table quickly across GPU costs {$2, $3.5, $6}, avg tokens {400, 800, 1600}, cache hits {10, 30, 50%}.
- Prototype UI wording for credits vs convos vs token-based billing.

Handy quick formulas (copyable):
- tokens_per_gpu_hour = throughput_tokens_per_sec * 3600
- gpu_cost_per_token = gpu_cost_per_hour / tokens_per_gpu_hour
- per_convo_compute_cost = gpu_cost_per_token * effective_tokens_per_convo * (1 + infra_overhead_pct)
- retail_price_per_convo_target = per_convo_compute_cost / desired_margin_pct

Random scribbles:
- If we want price parity with competitor X at $0.02/convo, we need to drive GPU cost down to ~$1.2/hr at current assumptions or push cache/batching to ~45–55% savings.
- Consider a tiny micro-tier for hobbyists: $7/mo -> 300 convos (trial culture).

End — rough and messy. Will refine after telemetry pull and a quick Monte Carlo on distribution.

-- Ethan
